question: Using determinants, obtain the equation of the line passing through $(1,-2)$ and $(4,4)$. Hence, determine the point at which it meets the $x$-axis.
explanation:
Determinant condition
For an arbitrary point $(x,y)$ on the line, $$\begin{vmatrix}x&y&1\\1&-2&1\\4&4&1\end{vmatrix}=0$$
Expansion and simplification
Expanding gives $$x(-2-4)-y(1-4)+(4+8)=0$$ Therefore, $$-6x+3y+12=0$$ or $$2x-y-4=0$$
Intersection with the $x$-axis
On the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Thus, $$2x-4=0$$ giving $x=2$.
Hence, the line meets the $x$-axis at $(2,0)$.
